# Multi-Provider Token Economics

Dimension 7 of the LLM Token Budgeting research. Covers pricing across providers,
context window differences, cost optimization through routing, and OpenRouter
mechanisms. Source details in [citations.md](../citations.md).

**Key pricing facts:**
- Output tokens cost 3-5× more than input tokens [27]
- Image tokens cost ~2× text; audio ~8× text [27]
- Open-source models ~90% cheaper than closed-source at same intelligence
  level [53]

## Price Trends

- LLM API prices dropped ~80% between early 2025 and early 2026 [35]
- GPT-4 equivalent performance: $20/MTok (late 2022) → ~$0.40 (2026) — 50×
  reduction [60]
- Price to achieve GPT-4 performance fell 40× per year [40]
- Token prices decreasing by factors of 10-1,000× per year (NeurIPS 2025) [60]

## Context Window Pricing Tiers

Not all context is priced equally [27]:
- Anthropic: flat pricing up to 200K; 1M windows available on select models
- Google: tiered — $1.25/MTok for ≤200K input, $2.50/MTok for >200K
- OpenAI: prompts exceeding certain thresholds charged at 2× input, 1.5× output

The stateless API model means full conversation history is resent each turn,
creating exponential cost growth in extended conversations. Multimedia (images)
in early turns incur vision processing fees on every subsequent turn [27].

## OpenRouter Mechanisms

### Provider Selection Algorithm [18]

1. **Stability filter**: Remove providers with outages in last 30 seconds
2. **Inverse-square price weighting**: $1 provider gets 9× more routing than
   $3 provider (calculated as 1/price²)
3. **Fallback**: Remaining providers as backup

### Model Fallbacks [19]

`models` parameter accepts array of model IDs in priority order. Automatic
failover on context length errors, content moderation, rate limiting, provider
downtime. Priced using model actually used [19].

### Pricing [36]

5.5% fee (minimum $0.80) for non-crypto; 5.0% flat for crypto. Access to
300+ models from all major providers [36].

### Configuration Options [18]

| Option | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `sort` | Prioritize by price, throughput, or latency |
| `order` | Specify preferred providers in sequence |
| `max_price` | Spending ceiling per request |
| `preferred_min_throughput` | Minimum token generation speed |
| `preferred_max_latency` | Maximum response time |
| `:nitro` suffix | Throughput optimization shortcut |
| `:floor` suffix | Price optimization shortcut |

## Cost Optimization Through Routing

| Strategy | Savings | Mechanism |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| Smart routing (general) | 30-85% [61] | Route to cheapest capable model |
| Hybrid routing | 37-46% [61] | Traditional methods for basic, LLM for complex |
| Semantic routing | 85% (maintaining 95% GPT-4 performance) [43] | Embeddings-based task classification |
| Model tiering | 50%+ | Route 60% of requests to cheaper model [43] |

Example: GPT-4o ($2.50/MTok) vs GPT-4o-mini ($0.15/MTok) is 16× difference.
Routing 60% of requests to the cheaper model cuts costs by >50% [43].

## The Cheapest Model Paradox

Selecting the lowest per-token cost often backfires. A more capable model may [27]:
- Understand simple prompts correctly on first attempt
- Generate concise, accurate responses without refinement
- Reduce cumulative token consumption despite higher per-token rates

Mistral Medium 3.1 delivers ≥90% of Claude Sonnet 3.7 performance at 8×
lower cost [54]. Optimize for total cost to achieve outcome, not per-token
price [27].

| Provider | Cache Read Cost | Cache Write Cost | Minimum Tokens |
|----------|----------------|------------------|----------------|
| Anthropic | 0.1× base (90% savings) [17] | 1.25× (5m) or 2× (1h) [17] | 1,024-4,096 [17] |
| OpenAI | 50% reduction [55] | Automatic [55] | — |
| Google | Varies | Varies | — |

Batch API provides additional 50%+ discount for non-urgent work. Combined
caching + batching achieves 95%+ total savings [55].
